title: quota-ledger 0.1 - core reservations and Postgres backend

overview.problemStatement: A process-local token bucket in wirekit cannot answer the question a multi-tenant service actually asks before an outbound provider call: may this tenant spend one more unit of this provider's quota right now, and what happens if they cannot? Without shared state, two API pods each believe they hold the last unit, a retry spends quota twice, and a restart forgets the month's consumption. Every service then invents its own ledger, and its own answer to reserve-then-fail.
overview.proposedSolution: Port and adapt the quota-ledger crate from feature/m3-substrate as prior art: TenantId, ProviderId, Metric, Window, Period, Budget, ExhaustionPolicy, QuotaKey, Reservation, ReserveRequest, ReserveOutcome, Usage, and QuotaExceeded, behind an async QuotaStore trait with reserve, commit, release, and usage. Ship MemoryQuotaStore for tests and single-process callers, and an optional postgres feature adding a transactional backend that uses an atomic conditional UPDATE so concurrent reservations cannot exceed a limit. No Redis backend in 0.1 (BP-019).
overview.targetAudience: Rust teams running more than one instance of a service that calls rate-limited or metered providers, and this project's service layer that brokers provider quota across pods.
assumptions: A working implementation exists on feature/m3-substrate (18 files, features default and postgres) and is ported and adapted rather than redesigned.
main has no [workspace.dependencies], and the branch manifests use dep.workspace = true, so async-trait, chrono, thiserror, uuid, sqlx, and platform-core are declared directly in the crate manifest.
Main depends on platform-core for TenantId and ProviderId identity; quota-ledger reuses that identity so a tenant is one tenant across the stack.
The branch tests are not ported; the test agent authors tests against this specification.
The unmerged m3-substrate/v1 spec covers four crates and is not reused as governance here.
outOfScope: A Redis backend; the catalogue leaves it as BP-019, a separate later item.
Process-local rate limiting; that remains the wirekit token bucket.
Billing, invoicing, and currency conversion; the ledger records consumption only.
A distributed lock service or consensus protocol.
A policy engine that decides pricing; the caller supplies the policy.
Any product or vendor workflow vocabulary (CON-106).

userStories.title: Key quota by tenant, provider, and metric
userStories.want: a typed key that names whose quota, which provider, and which unit
userStories.benefit: one ledger can hold every provider's meter without collisions

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given a tenant, provider, and metric, when a QuotaKey is constructed, then it identifies exactly one budget line and two different metrics for one provider are separate lines.
Given the crate built with --no-default-features, when it compiles, then the core types, error type, and memory store are available without the postgres feature.

userStories.title: Reserve, then commit or release
userStories.want: to hold quota before a call and settle it after
userStories.benefit: two pods cannot spend the same last unit and a failed call does not burn quota

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given capacity remaining, when reserve is called, then it returns a reservation with an identifier and the held amount without consuming it.
Given an open reservation, when commit is called, then it consumes the hold exactly once, and a second commit for the same reservation is rejected or idempotent and never consumes twice.
Given an open reservation, when release is called, then the held amount returns to the available budget.
Given no capacity remaining and a policy of HardStop, when reserve is called, then it is denied with a typed QuotaExceeded carrying the reset instant and does not create a reservation.

userStories.title: Idempotent reservations under retry
userStories.want: a retried reserve to return the original reservation
userStories.benefit: a lost response does not hold quota twice

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given a caller idempotency key already used with the same payload, when reserve is called again, then the existing reservation is returned and no second hold is taken.
Given a caller idempotency key previously used with a different payload, when reserve is called, then it fails with a typed idempotency-conflict error rather than returning the wrong reservation.

userStories.title: Apply an exhaustion policy
userStories.want: to choose what happens when a budget runs out
userStories.benefit: the ledger enforces the decision instead of each caller inventing one

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given a budget, when ExhaustionPolicy is inspected, then it distinguishes HardStop, Overage, Degrade, and Queue, and HardStop denies while the others report the outcome the caller asked for.

userStories.title: Report usage and the next reset
userStories.want: to read limit, used, held, and the next reset
userStories.benefit: a dashboard and a caller both see the same truth

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given a key with reservations, when usage is read, then it reports the limit, the consumed amount, the held amount, and the next reset instant.
Given a window period, when it is configured, then Daily, Monthly, and Rolling windows are supported and the reset instant is computed from the window rather than assumed to be UTC midnight.

userStories.title: Share the ledger across processes
userStories.want: the postgres backend behind the same trait
userStories.benefit: quota survives restarts and is consistent across pods

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given the postgres feature, when the backend is built, then it implements QuotaStore over a connection and its schema is shipped as SQL the caller applies.
Given concurrent reservations from many tasks against one limited budget, when all complete, then the total committed never exceeds the limit.

userStories.title: Isolate tenants and build on 1.87
userStories.want: tenant scoping and the workspace baseline enforced
userStories.benefit: one tenant can never read or spend another's quota

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given a tenant, when usage or a reservation is read, then no key can observe another tenant's usage, and every store operation is scoped by the tenant in the key.

Given the crate, when it is built with all features on Rust 1.87, then it compiles with forbid(unsafe_code) and deny(missing_docs), ships the licence files, and every Postgres statement is parameterized rather than string-interpolated.

functionalRequirements.text: The crate MUST expose TenantId, ProviderId, Metric, Window, Period, Budget, ExhaustionPolicy, QuotaKey, Reservation, ReservationId, ReserveRequest, ReserveOutcome, Usage, and QuotaExceeded per catalogue/29_quota.md.
Features MUST be additive and default to none; a --no-default-features build MUST compile the core without Postgres.
QuotaStore MUST be async and cover reserve, commit, release, and usage.
commit MUST consume a hold exactly once; a repeated commit MUST NOT spend quota twice.

A reservation MUST carry an optional caller idempotency key; a repeated key with the same payload MUST return the existing reservation and a repeated key with a different payload MUST fail as a conflict.
A denial MUST be a typed QuotaExceeded carrying the reset instant, never a generic error.
ExhaustionPolicy MUST distinguish HardStop, Overage, Degrade, and Queue.
Window and Period MUST support daily, monthly, and rolling windows and compute the reset instant from the configured window.
A postgres feature MUST add a QuotaStore implementation backed by a shipped schema and must be absent when the feature is off.
The postgres backend MUST use an atomic conditional statement so concurrent reservations cannot exceed the limit.
Every store operation MUST be scoped by the tenant carried in the key.
The crate MUST declare forbid(unsafe_code) and deny(missing_docs), and MUST NOT introduce a second error type (CON-207 analogue for a standalone crate).

nonFunctionalRequirements.text: No API may return or spend another tenant's quota; every operation is scoped by the tenant and provider key (CON-512).
Every Postgres statement MUST be parameterized; no query may interpolate caller values into SQL text (CON-516).
All caller-supplied keys, metrics, and windows MUST be validated before use, and an invalid window MUST produce a positioned error rather than a guessed default (CON-515).
The crate MUST NOT read credentials from the environment or a file; the caller supplies the connection (CON-519), and a Postgres connection MUST require TLS (CON-520).
The crate MUST compile on Rust 1.87 with all features and MUST contain no product or vendor workflow vocabulary (CON-102, CON-106).
Every public item MUST carry rustdoc and every module MUST state its scope and non-goals (CON-202, CON-203).

edgeCases.description: Concurrent reserve calls race for the final unit
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: Exactly one succeeds; the others are denied. The total committed never exceeds the limit.

edgeCases.description: Process crashes between reserve and commit
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: The hold remains and is reclaimable after the reservation TTL; the ledger never silently consumes it.

edgeCases.description: Idempotency key replayed with a different metric or amount
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: Typed idempotency-conflict error; no second reservation is created.
The reservation settles against the window it was created in; the reset instant is derived from the window, not the host clock's midnight.
Core compiles with no sqlx in the dependency graph.

dependencies.name: platform-core

dependencies.notes: Async QuotaStore methods; declared directly because main has no workspace.dependencies.

dependencies.name: chrono
dependencies.notes: Window start/end and the reset instant.

risks.description: The postgres backend is the hardest part to verify without a live database, so a defect in the atomic claim may pass review.
risks.mitigation: AC-013 asserts the concurrency invariant directly, and the branch already ships a postgres test harness to adapt.

risks.description: Porting stale code may drag in manifests using workspace inheritance the current workspace does not define.
risks.mitigation: Adapt the manifest to declare dependencies directly, as platform-core did, and let the MSRV and clippy jobs prove it.

risks.description: A quota ledger invites scope creep into billing and pricing.
risks.mitigation: The out-of-scope list and NFR-005 are enforced at review; the catalogue's non-goals are copied verbatim.
